newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas prices strengthen on warm forecast.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas prices strengthen on warm forecast.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices turned stronger Thursday as warmer weather was forecast for most of the U.S. this weekend, sources said.
"There are bullish tones in the market," one trader said, noting more buyers were expected to emerge on Monday.

On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, swing prices at the Henry Hub were quoted up four to five cents to $2.21-2.25/mmBtu, while baseload prices were also higher at $2.20-2.235. On Transco (Station 65), deals were reported done as high as $2.27.
For the weekend, gas sold at the Hub at $2.24, a trader said.
Temperatures in Houston were expected to rise to a high of 94 degrees F by Saturday, Weather Services Corp reported, while highs in Dallas were forecast around 95 degrees F.
The anticipated jump in temperatures also propped up prices in south Texas, where prices were quoted a few cents higher in the mid-to-high teens for Friday delivery.

In the Midwest, where temperatures are expected to reach highs around 90 degrees F by the weekend, swing prices for Friday were talked higher at $2.12-2.16, up more than five cents from August indices and about 10 cents higher than July indices.
Chicago city-gate gas for Friday was talked around $2.30, also up more than five cents from Wednesday's discussion.
In the Permian Basin market, August was quoted at $2.05-2.13, with most business reported done around $2.10. San Juan was said to be holding at $2.00-2.03.
"No utilities are buying yet. They'll probably come out Monday," one trader said, referring to the San Juan basin market.
Also, the 750 megawatt Four Corners unit 5 in New Mexico was expected to return to service Sunday, the operator Arizona Public Service said earlier today.
In the East, New York city gate gas was also holding in the low-$2.40s, traders said.
